newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL TO INVESTIGATE CORDERO.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL TO INVESTIGATE CORDERO.

text.p: Major League Baseball said Friday it would investigate Boston Red Sox outfielder Wil Cordero after allegations surfaced of wife-beating years before an incident for which he currently faces charges.

"Allegations of domestic abuse and domestic violence are to be taken extremely seriously," said acting commissioner Bud Selig. "There is no room in baseball or society for such behaviour and we in baseball abhor it."
Red Sox management was considering dropping the player.

"We're looking at a very limited set of choices here, and our choices aren't very attractive," Red Sox general manager Dan Duquette said at a news conference Friday. "We wanted to do the right thing for Wilfredo and (wife) Ana and their family, and also the community. Releasing him is one of our options and it is being considered."
The 25-year-old Cordero took batting practice before Friday night's game against Detroit at Fenway Park, but was not in uniform for the game.
"The official Red Sox stance will be that he will not be in uniform for the game tonight," said manager Jimy Williams. "We will take this on a game-to-game basis."

Cordero had been slated Thursday night to make his first start at home since being charged earlier this month with abusing his second wife, but was scratched from the lineup in the light of a Boston Globe report of abuse charges made against Cordero by his first wife dating back to 1990-93.
The accusations, which were included in a court document obtained by the newspaper, claimed Cordero beat Wanda Mora Cordero repeatedly, including while she was pregnant.

Cordero had appeared in six road games for the Red Sox since he was arrested June 11 on charges of battering his second wife, Ana Echevarria. He pleaded innocent to charges of assault with a dangerous weapon and assault and battery. His wife refused to testify against him, although prosecutors are continuing their investigation.
A pre-trial hearing is scheduled for July 24.
A pre-game meeting Thursday involving Cordero, Williams and Duquette lasted into the first inning before the outfielder left the ballpark, escorted by security.

All of the allegations made by Wanda Cordero in the 1993 document occurred while Cordero was with the Montreal Expos organisation, for whom Duquette was an executive at the time. It was Duquette who engineered Boston's acquisition of Cordero just prior to the 1996 season.
But Duquette said Friday he had no knowledge of any past domestic problems involving Cordero, adding that any employee-counsellor relations would have been kept confidential from management.
The Red Sox said Thursday that no one in the organisation, including Duquette, had knowledge of any past domestic problems involving Cordero.

Cordero, primarily an infielder in past years, spent the 1990 season with Jacksonville of the Southern League and the 1991 and 1992 campaigns with Indianapolis of the American Association before joining the Expos at the end of 1992.
